answers.answer: In the 3-player example the tied lead earns no coin; the sole last player pays 1 coin. In a 2-player unequal Census, the unique leader still gains 1 coin, but the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Census: ‘a tied lead gives no coin’; ‘In a 2-player game the last player never pays’.

answers.answer: No. You may draw any number up to the allowance, limited by free Market spaces, so you may draw at most two. Unused Followers remain on the Market between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Followers: ‘Draw any number up to the allowance … limited by free Market spaces’; unused Market Followers ‘occupy capacity’.

answers.answer: Yes, an action may be filled gradually over multiple rounds. It cannot be activated until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs only one of its two spaces). A fully activated action may be saved for a later round. When executed, its Followers return to your bag; Technology stays in place.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Planning/Actions: ‘fill an action gradually over multiple rounds’; ‘An activation can be saved’; after execution Followers return to the bag and Technology stays.

answers.answer: Beginning with the Start Player and proceeding clockwise repeatedly, each player takes one activated action or passes. Passing ends that player's participation for the Action Phase, so they cannot act again that round. Unused activations retain their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Actions: ‘taking one activated action or passing’; ‘Passing ends your participation’; unused activations keep their Followers on the board.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at that space.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Farm House: ‘Put a new Farmer in your bag; advance Farmers Track one space and take its depicted good.’

answers.answer: Village lets you recruit one Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader into your bag and advance that profession's track. Boatman gives the depicted coins, except the first player at the last space gets a Citizen instead. Craftsman gives a Technology tile, usable only after you pass. Trader gives a Place Tile: first advance allows category I only; later advances allow I or II.
answers.evidence: Actions, Village recruitment: the three recruit options and their distinct track rewards are listed.

answers.answer: No. A newly acquired Technology can be used only after you pass, so it cannot help execute another action that round after that pass. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. Later Technology may replace any profession except Monk. At most one Technology may be placed at a Place, and none at a Place requiring only one Follower. It permanently fills that space and cannot be moved. A Craftsman-acquired tile is used only after passing.
answers.evidence: Actions, Technology: first tile replaces a Farmer; later ones any profession except Monk; placement limits and permanence. Village recruitment says Craftsman Technology is used only after passing.

answers.answer: No. The first Trader-track advance permits category I only; each later advance permits category I or II. Players may inspect the Place Tile stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Actions, Village recruitment and Setup: first Trader advance ‘category I only’; later I or II; players may inspect stacks at any time.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances the Scholars Track one space, and grants its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances the Knights Track; that track sets future draw allowance. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. The fourth Knight does not increase the allowance beyond 7; the first player there gets the Citizen. Once a character track is on its last space, that corresponding action cannot be taken again.
answers.evidence: Actions table gives University, Castle and Monastery effects; Character-track limits: fourth Knight does not raise allowance above 7 and actions stop at the last space.

answers.answer: A Monk may replace a Knight on an ordinary action. A Knight or Technology cannot replace a required Monk. A Monk cannot replace the exact profession shown on a Beneficial Deed.
answers.evidence: Actions, Monks: Monk replaces any profession, but no Follower or Technology replaces a required Monk. Town Hall: Deeds require exact professions; substitutions including Monks cannot replace them.

answers.answer: One Ship or Wagon action moves the Merchant along exactly one adjacent Waterway or Road connection. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if multiple lie there. An empty connection is legal and yields no good.
answers.evidence: Actions, Movement and goods: ‘One Ship/Wagon action traverses just one connection’; may take ‘one good’; empty connections are legal.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one of your Trading Stations in the town where your Merchant currently is. A town with any player's station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one station.
answers.evidence: Actions, Building: Merchant must be in the town; occupied towns cannot receive another station; Orléans exception allows one per player.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gives 1 Development Point by moving one space on the Development Track. When Development movement lands on or passes a coin space, collect its coins; the first player onto or past a Citizen space takes that Citizen; reaching or passing a Development Status space immediately changes your Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table, Scriptorium; Scoring: moving ‘onto or past’ coin/Citizen spaces grants rewards, and reaching/passing a Status space updates Status immediately.

answers.answer: Town Hall can activate with one eligible Follower and can send one or two Followers in one action. Your four marked starting Followers cannot be used. Send them to free Deed spaces matching their exact professions, possibly on different Deeds. Each placement gives the depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; Canalization gives a choice of 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The player filling a Deed's last empty space takes its Citizen. Followers remain there for the game.
answers.evidence: Actions table says Town Hall needs 1 or 2 eligible Followers. Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds section states starting Followers barred, exact-profession destinations, rewards, Canalization choice and Citizen for completing a Deed.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment during that round's Phase 5 Action Phase; the restriction applies before the Event Phase. Other events resolve in Phase 6. The game opens with Pilgrimage because it is placed on top of the Hour Glass stack.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5; Event is Phase 6. Setup: Pilgrimage is put on top so round 1 always has it.

answers.answer: Only grain, cheese, or wine count as food; wool does not. Paid food goes to the Goods Market. If you have no food, you owe 5 coins; if you have fewer than five, you pay the available coins and undergo torture for each missing coin.
answers.evidence: Events, Harvest: pay grain, cheese, or wine to Goods Market; otherwise pay 5 coins, and inability to pay causes torture for the shortfall. Wool and brocade are not food.

answers.answer: The neutral Scholar is returned to its game-board supply and becomes recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. The colored starting Trader is kept, so no starting Follower is lost and you do not redraw.
answers.evidence: Events, Plague: neutral Followers return to their supply without moving the marker back; marked starting Followers are kept and not redrawn.

answers.answer: Pay the one available coin, then replace each of the two missing coins with an item, using any mix of the listed choices: a built or unbuilt Trading Station, a random eligible neutral Follower drawn from your bag, one Development Point moved left, a Goods Tile, Place Tile, or Technology tile. For a Follower sacrifice, return and redraw marked starting Followers until you draw an eligible neutral one. A lost Development Point cannot move onto or past a coin space. Surrendered items are removed from the game, not returned to supply; only lost Development Points can be regained. Marked starting Followers are never lost or paid.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Torture: lists eligible payment items and restrictions, states surrendered items are removed, and marked starting Followers always stay with you.

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods Tile, even if another part of the action would still reward you. It becomes available again when the required tile returns to stock, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply is insufficient, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Special Rules, Limited supplies: unavailable-tile action restriction, availability restored when stock returns, and insufficient coin supply means no coins received then.

answers.answer: With a tie for most built Trading Stations, nobody gets the bonus Citizen. Goods are worth grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, brocade 5 points each. Built stations and collected Citizens score (number of built stations + number of Citizens) × final Development Status. Equal scores are broken by who is furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, players share victory.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: unique most stations takes the Citizen, ties give nobody; goods values, station/Citizen formula and tie breakers are stated there.
